items.claim: An IDOR/BOLA finding is only validated with two identities the tester controls, because a hardware serial number seen on the device proves nothing about the server-side ownership check on the object id.
items.body:
An IDOR/BOLA finding is only validated with two identities the tester controls, because a hardware serial number seen on the device proves nothing about the server-side ownership check on the object id.

HackTricks reference: Wi-Fi Direct, Aware, AWDL and IoT Provisioning (generic-methodologies-and-resources/pentesting-wifi/wifi-direct-and-iot-provisioning.md)
items.disproof: A validation run in which the second identity is not under the tester's control, or in which access is judged from a device serial number instead of a cross-account request against the object id, refutes this requirement.

sources.quote: Validate IDOR/BOLA only with two accounts/devices you control; a serial number is not proof of ownership.
If an attacker can use the `GET` (or another) method to perform actions on a restricted URL, they can bypass the access control that is implemented at the platform layer.

items.claim: IDOR/BOLA needs two things at once: an endpoint that accepts a user-controllable object id, and the absence of any check that the caller may access or modify the object that id resolves to.
items.body:
IDOR/BOLA needs two things at once: an endpoint that accepts a user-controllable object id, and the absence of any check that the caller may access or modify the object that id resolves to.

HackTricks reference: IDOR (pentesting-web/idor.md)
items.disproof: An endpoint that accepts an attacker-supplied object id but still refuses cross-account access with 403 or 404 because it verifies the caller's ownership refutes the missing-authorization half of the claim.

sources.quote: Insecure direct object references (IDOR) are a type of access control vulnerability that arises when an application uses user-supplied input to access objects directly.

items.claim: IDOR coverage comes from pairing a forced-browse / auth-matrix pass that maps which roles may reach each endpoint with bulk sweeps of collected object ids, rather than probing one identifier at a time by hand.
items.body:
IDOR coverage comes from pairing a forced-browse / auth-matrix pass that maps which roles may reach each endpoint with bulk sweeps of collected object ids, rather than probing one identifier at a time by hand.

HackTricks reference: IDOR (pentesting-web/idor.md)
items.disproof: A hunt that only issues single-id probes, or that never maps roles to endpoints, refutes this pairing as the thing that actually produces IDOR coverage.
